author: implementation-agent

findings.summary: Backend path validation uses a narrower control-character policy than the established route-segment safety helpers.
findings.consequence: A decoded backend path containing a C1 control such as U+0085 is accepted and forwarded as a percent-encoded upstream path even though sibling proxy and route validation code treats C1 controls as unsafe; future proxy hardening can drift further because the same path-segment boundary has multiple implementations.
findings.evidence: The owned callback rejects only code points <= 31 and 127. Current sibling path-boundary code in server/routes/red/[...path].ts and server/utils/reader-source-proxy.ts calls shared hasC0OrC1Control plus hasLoneSurrogate for proxy path segments, and shared/utils/route-segment.ts applies the same C1/lone-surrogate policy for validated route segments. The packet-listed test/unit/backend-proxy.spec.ts rejection table covers NUL, U+001F, and U+007F but has no C1 or lone-surrogate backend-path case.
findings.recommendation: Use the shared text-safety helpers inside safeBackendPath, or extract a shared proxy path-segment validator used by backend, red, and reader-source proxies, so C0, C1, delete, and malformed Unicode are governed by one policy.
